module.title: Pricing
module.description: Sales prices of articles: proposing them, approving them and expiring them. It makes sure a sales price is never below the purchase price. Discounts per customer are out of scope (see DEC-001).

userStory.raw: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to propose a sales price for an article, so that it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay.
userStory.goal: propose a sales price for an article
userStory.benefit: it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay

sections.Summary and user story: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to propose a sales price for an article, so that it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay.
sections.Business value / problem: New articles and changed purchase prices get a sales price quickly, and never one below the purchase price.
sections.Preconditions and triggers: An article was activated (EVT-ARTICLE-ACTIVATED) or one of its purchase prices changed (EVT-PURCHASE-PRICE-CHANGED). The article appears on SCR-PRC-01 as waiting for a sales price.
sections.Main flow:
1. On SCR-PRC-01, the pricing manager opens an article waiting for a sales price.
2. They see its valid purchase prices and its current sales price, if any.
3. They use action A01 Propose and enter the amount and the valid-from date.
4. The amount is checked against the highest valid purchase price (RULE-PRC-001).
5. The sales price is saved as proposed and waits for approval.
sections.Alternative and exception flows:
- The amount is not higher than the highest valid purchase price: nothing is saved and the pricing manager sees the purchase price (RULE-PRC-001).
- The article is no longer active: nothing is saved (RULE-001).
- A proposed sales price already exists for the article: it is replaced by the new proposal.
sections.Data in / data out: In: article, amount, valid-from date. Shown: valid purchase prices, current sales price. Out: a proposed sales price.
sections.Business rules applied:
- RULE-001 — only active articles get a sales price.
- RULE-PRC-001 — the amount must be higher than the highest valid purchase price.
sections.State transitions caused: None. A new sales price starts as proposed.
sections.Notifications: None. The proposal appears on SCR-PRC-01 for approval.
sections.Permissions and data visibility: Pricing managers propose sales prices for all articles. Sales staff never see proposed prices.
sections.Acceptance criteria:
### CAP-PRC-001-AC-01

- **Given** an active article whose highest valid purchase price is 8.00
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price of 10.00
- **Then** the sales price is saved as proposed
- **Covers:** main flow step 5

### CAP-PRC-001-AC-02

- **Given** an active article whose highest valid purchase price is 8.00
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price of 7.50
- **Then** nothing is saved and the pricing manager sees the purchase price of 8.00
- **Covers:** RULE-PRC-001

### CAP-PRC-001-AC-03

- **Given** a discontinued article
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price
- **Then** nothing is saved
- **Covers:** RULE-001
sections.Out of scope:
- Prices per customer group (DEC-001).
- Promotions and temporary discounts.

personas.title: Pricing analyst
personas.description:
**Goals:** sales prices that cover the purchase price and are approved before anyone uses them.

**Pain points:** learns about purchase price increases weeks later.

entities.title: Article
entities.description: Something the company sells. Sales staff only ever see active articles.

attributes.name: Unit of measure
attributes.description: The unit it is sold in

entities.title: Purchase price
entities.description: What a supplier charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date.

entities.title: Sales price
entities.description: What the company charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date.

rules.title: Only active articles are sold
rules.statement: An article can have a valid sales price, and be shown to sales staff, only while it is active.

rules.title: Sales price covers the purchase price
rules.statement: A sales price must be higher than the highest valid purchase price of the same article.

events.title: Article activated
events.description: An article became active. Pricing is told so a sales price can be proposed.

events.title: Purchase price changed
events.description: A new purchase price became valid. Pricing checks whether the sales price still covers it.

screens.title: Sales price review
screens.purpose: Work through articles that need a sales price, proposals that need approval, and discontinued articles whose prices must expire.

glossary.definition: Something the company sells, identified by its article number.
What a supplier charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date.
What the company charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date, once approved.

openQuestions.title: Do sales prices differ per customer group?
openQuestions.context:
**Context:** Some customers get better prices today, agreed outside any system. Until this is decided, an article
has one valid sales price at a time.
